records.source: Παῦλος καὶ Σιλουανὸς καὶ Τιμόθεος τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ Θεσσαλονικέων ἐν θεῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ·
records.gloss: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of [the] Thessalonians in God Father of us and Lord Jesus Christ;
pieces: From Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians, which belongs to God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.1: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.1: This letter is from Paul, Silvanus and Timothy. We are writing to the church in the city of Thessalonica. You belong to God our Father and to the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: the same senders and church as 1 Thessalonians
decisions.reason: The opening repeats 1 Thessalonians 1:1 almost word for word. This letter follows up the first: the church is still under pressure (1:4), and some are now troubled by a claim that the day of the Lord has already come (2:1-2).

decisions.choice: in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: the church lives in union with them
decisions.reason: As in 1 Thessalonians 1:1, one preposition covers God and Jesus together; here Paul adds "our" Father.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: which belongs to
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "in God" means here (m2).

records.heading: Greeting

records.source: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: Grace to you and peace from God Father and Lord Jesus Christ.
pieces: Grace and peace to you from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.2: Grace to you and peace from God [the] Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.2: We pray that God the Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will show you grace and give you peace.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "God the Father"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "God our Father", as in verse 1 and Paul's other greetings. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: We pray that God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ will show you grace and give you peace
alternatives: Grace to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Readable makes the greeting a prayer, as in 1 Thessalonians 1:1.

records.source: Εὐχαριστεῖν ὀφείλομεν τῷ θεῷ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοί, καθὼς ἄξιόν ἐστιν, ὅτι ὑπεραυξάνει ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν καὶ πλεονάζει ἡ ἀγάπη ἑνὸς ἑκάστου πάντων ὑμῶν εἰς ἀλλήλους, ὥστε αὐτοὺς ἡμᾶς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐγκαυχᾶσθαι ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τοῦ θεοῦ ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑπομονῆς ὑμῶν καὶ πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς διωγμοῖς ὑμῶν καὶ ταῖς θλίψεσιν αἷς ἀνέχεσθε, ἔνδειγμα τῆς δικαίας κρίσεως τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ καταξιωθῆναι ὑμᾶς τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, ὑπὲρ ἧς καὶ πάσχετε, εἴπερ δίκαιον παρὰ θεῷ ἀνταποδοῦναι τοῖς θλίβουσιν ὑμᾶς θλῖψιν καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς θλιβομένοις ἄνεσιν μεθ’ ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἀποκαλύψει τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ μετ’ ἀγγέλων δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ ἐν φλογὶ πυρός, διδόντος ἐκδίκησιν τοῖς μὴ εἰδόσι θεὸν καὶ τοῖς μὴ ὑπακούουσιν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ, οἵτινες δίκην τίσουσιν ὄλεθρον αἰώνιον ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ, ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐνδοξασθῆναι ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ καὶ θαυμασθῆναι ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς πιστεύσασιν, ὅτι ἐπιστεύθη τὸ μαρτύριον ἡμῶν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ.
records.gloss: To give thanks we ought to the God always concerning you, brothers, just as fitting it is, because grows exceedingly the faith of you and increases the love of one each of all of you toward one another, \v 4 so that ourselves us in you to boast in the churches of the God for the endurance of you and faith in all the persecutions of you and the afflictions which you are bearing, \v 5 evidence of the just judgment of the God, so that to be counted worthy you of the kingdom of the God, for which also you suffer, \v 6 since [it is] just with God to repay to those afflicting you affliction \v 7 and to you, the [ones] being afflicted, relief with us at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with angels of power of him \v 8 in flame of fire, giving vengeance to those not knowing God and to those not obeying the gospel of the Lord of us Jesus, \v 9 who [the] penalty will pay, destruction eternal, away from [the] face of the Lord and from the glory of the strength of him, \v 10 when he comes to be glorified in the holy [ones] of him and to be marveled at in all those having believed, because was believed the testimony of us to you, in the day that.
pieces: We are bound to thank God for you at all times, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, and rightly so, because your faith is growing beyond measure and the love every one of you has for the others keeps increasing.
So we ourselves speak proudly of you among the churches of God, because of your endurance and faith in all the persecutions and troubles you are bearing.
All this is evidence that God judges rightly, and the result will be that you are counted worthy of God's kingdom, for which you are suffering.
For it is right for God to repay with suffering those who make you suffer,
and to give rest to you who suffer, as to us also, when the Lord Jesus appears from heaven with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty angels
in a blaze of fire, bringing punishment on those who do not know God and on those who refuse to obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus.
They will pay the penalty of eternal destruction, cut off from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power,

on that day when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to be glorified among {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people and marveled at by all who believed. And you are among those believers, for when we bore witness to you, you believed it.

L.3: We ought always to give thanks to God for you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, as is fitting, because your faith is growing greatly and the love of each one of you all for one another is increasing,
L.4: so that we ourselves boast about you in the churches of God for your endurance and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions that you are bearing.
L.5: [This is] evidence of the just judgment of God, so that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are also suffering,
L.6: since [it is] just in God's sight to repay with affliction those who afflict you,
L.7: and [to give] relief to you who are afflicted, along with us, at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power
L.8: in flaming fire, inflicting vengeance on those who do not know God and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus.
L.9: They will pay the penalty, eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} might,
L.10: when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to be glorified in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy ones and to be marveled at among all who have believed (because our testimony to you was believed) on that day.

R.3: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, we should always thank God for you. It is right for us to do this, because your faith is growing more and more, and every one of you loves the others more and more.
R.4: So we tell all of God's churches how proud we are of you. We tell them how you keep going and keep your faith, even though people are hurting you and you are going through hard times.
R.5: This shows that God judges fairly. God will count you worthy to be part of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom, the kingdom you are suffering for.
R.6: God is fair. He will pay back with trouble the people who are troubling you.
R.7: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give rest to you who are suffering, and to us too. This will happen when the Lord Jesus comes from heaven with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} powerful angels
R.8: in flames of fire. He will punish those who do not know God and those who do not obey the good news about our Lord Jesus.
R.9: Their punishment will be eternal destruction. They will be shut out from the Lord's presence and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious power
R.10: on the day when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes. On that day all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people will give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory, and all who have believed will be amazed at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And you will be among them, because you believed what we told you.

decisions.choice: we ought to give thanks: a duty, gladly owned
decisions.reason: ὀφείλομεν ("we ought") speaks of an obligation: their growth makes thanks the only fitting response, ἄξιόν ἐστιν ("as is fitting").

decisions.choice: faith growing, love increasing: Paul's earlier prayer answered
decisions.reason: In 1 Thessalonians 3:10-12 Paul prayed that their faith would be supplied and their love increase. ὑπεραυξάνω is a strong word: growing beyond measure.

decisions.choice: evidence of God's just judgment: their faithful endurance under suffering shows that God's coming judgment will be just
alternatives: the persecution itself is a sign that judgment is coming on the persecutors
decisions.reason: ἔνδειγμα stands loosely after verse 4 and most naturally refers to the whole situation: their faith holding firm in suffering is a sign that God is at work and will judge rightly, vindicating them and repaying their persecutors (verses 6-7; Philippians 1:28).

decisions.choice: counted worthy of the kingdom: declared fit by God, not earning it
decisions.reason: καταξιόω means to count or declare worthy. Their suffering for the kingdom marks them as belonging to it (compare verse 11).

decisions.choice: God's justice repays: affliction to those who afflict, relief to the afflicted
decisions.reason: Paul leaves repayment to God, who alone judges rightly (Romans 12:19). The relief (ἄνεσιν, rest) is for Paul and his companions too.

decisions.choice: the revelation of the Lord Jesus: his unveiling, when he comes
decisions.reason: ἀποκαλύψει is an unveiling: Jesus, now hidden from sight, will be seen (1 Corinthians 1:7).

decisions.choice: in flaming fire: the fire of God's appearing
decisions.reason: God appeared in a flame of fire at the bush (Exodus 3:2) and "will come in fire" to judge (Isaiah 66:15). Some manuscripts reverse the two nouns ("in fire of flame"); the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: vengeance: punishment that puts wrong right
decisions.reason: ἐκδίκησιν is justice carried out on wrongdoers, which belongs to God (Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:19). Here Jesus carries it out.

decisions.choice: those who do not know God and those who do not obey the gospel
decisions.reason: The repeated article could mark two groups (Gentiles who do not know God, Jeremiah 10:25, and those who reject the gospel) or describe one group in two ways. Either way, the punishment is for refusing God.

decisions.choice: away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his might: Isaiah 2:10, 2:19, 2:21
alternatives: destruction coming from the Lord's presence
decisions.reason: The words echo Isaiah 2, where people hide "from the presence of the LORD and from the glory of his majesty". ἀπὸ can mean separation ("away from") or source ("coming from"). The echo of Isaiah suggests being banished from the Lord's presence, the opposite of being "with the Lord" for ever (1 Thessalonians 4:17).

decisions.choice: eternal destruction: ruin that belongs to the age to come and has no end
decisions.reason: ὄλεθρον is ruin, as in 1 Thessalonians 5:3; αἰώνιον ties it to the age to come, as "eternal life" is.

decisions.choice: because our testimony was believed: the Thessalonians are among those believers
decisions.reason: The clause breaks into the sentence to include the readers: the "all who have believed" of that day will include them, because they believed what Paul told them.

decisions.choice: to be glorified in his holy ones: his glory seen in his people
alternatives: to be glorified by his holy ones
decisions.reason: ἐν ("in") most naturally means his glory will shine in and through his people, as in verse 12; it may also mean "among them".

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: cut off from (B); shut out from (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m10, which is uncertain; Literal keeps "away from".

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable divide the sentence and put the clause about the Thessalonians at the end
alternatives: one sentence from verse 3 to verse 10
decisions.reason: The Greek runs from verse 3 to verse 10 as one sentence. Balanced and Readable divide it into shorter sentences and move the clause about the readers (m12) to the end, where it reads naturally.

records.heading: Thanks, and God's just judgment

records.source: εἰς ὃ καὶ προσευχόμεθα πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν, ἵνα ὑμᾶς ἀξιώσῃ τῆς κλήσεως ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν καὶ πληρώσῃ πᾶσαν εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης καὶ ἔργον πίστεως ἐν δυνάμει, ὅπως ἐνδοξασθῇ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν αὐτῷ, κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: for which also we pray always for you, that you may count worthy of the calling the God of us and may fulfill every desire of goodness and work of faith with power, \v 12 so that may be glorified the name of the Lord of us Jesus in you, and you in him, according to the grace of the God of us and Lord Jesus Christ.
pieces: With this in view we pray for you constantly. We ask our God to count you worthy of the life {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called you to, and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power to fulfill every good desire you have and every work your faith takes on.
Then the name of our Lord Jesus will be honored in you, and you will be honored in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, by the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.11: To this end we also pray always for you, that our God may count you worthy of the calling and fulfill every desire for goodness and work of faith with power,
L.12: so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, according to the grace of our God and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.11: So we always pray for you. We ask our God to make you worthy of the life {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has called you to live. We ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to use {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power to help you do all the good things you want to do, and all the things your faith leads you to do.
R.12: Then people will honor the name of our Lord Jesus because of you, and you will be honored because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. All this comes from the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: to this end: with that day in view
decisions.reason: εἰς ὃ looks back to verse 10: Paul prays that they will be ready to share in Christ's glory.

decisions.choice: count worthy: consider and declare worthy
decisions.reason: ἀξιόω usually means to consider worthy. The prayer asks God to find them worthy of the calling he gave them (1 Thessalonians 2:12).

decisions.choice: every desire for goodness: their own desire to do good
decisions.reason: εὐδοκίαν can be God's good pleasure or a person's desire. Joined with "work of faith", it is most likely their desire to do good, which God brings to completion by his power.

decisions.choice: glorified in you, and you in him: each honored in the other
decisions.reason: Christ's name is honored through his people, and they share his honor (1:10).

decisions.choice: the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ: two persons, as in verse 2
alternatives: the grace of our God and Lord, Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: One article covers both nouns, which could mean that Jesus Christ is called "our God and Lord". But "Lord Jesus Christ" is used almost as a name, which often goes without the article, and verse 2 names God and the Lord Jesus Christ as two. Both readings are possible.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the life {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called you to (B); the life {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has called you to live (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the calling" is: the life God called them to.

decisions.choice: honored
decisions.reason: The verb here is not the key term for "glorify"; "honored" fits the mutual honor of m4.
